sources: Written by Bantay in plain words from DailyMed and openFDA drug labels (US National Library of Medicine and US FDA, public domain) and NIH Office of Dietary Supplements fact sheets (public domain). No text is copied. This is not a full list of side effects or interactions.

cards.name: Amlodipine
cards.forWhat: Blood pressure and chest pain from the heart
cards.what: Amlodipine relaxes your blood vessels so blood flows with less push. It also helps the heart with chest pain.
how: Take it once a day, at the same time each day, with or without food.
Keep taking it when you feel well. High blood pressure often has no signs.
cards.missed: Take it when you remember, unless it is almost time for the next one. Never take two at once.
side: Swollen ankles or feet.
Flushing, headache or feeling tired in the first weeks.
Dizzy when you stand up fast. Stand up slowly.
cards.emergency: Chest pain that is new or worse, fainting, or trouble breathing: call 911.
noMix: Simvastatin: the simvastatin dose should stay low with amlodipine. Ask your doctor.
Large amounts of grapefruit juice.
Other blood pressure pills, unless your doctor planned it.
cards.food: Use herbs, calamansi and vinegar instead of salt. Less salt helps this medicine work better.
cards.generic: Generic name: amlodipine besylate. Brand names you may see: Norvasc.

cards.name: Losartan
cards.forWhat: Blood pressure, and it protects the kidneys in some people with diabetes
cards.what: Losartan relaxes your blood vessels so blood flows with less push. In some people it also protects the kidneys.
how: Take it once a day, at the same time each day, with or without food.
Keep taking it when you feel well.
It is not safe in pregnancy. Tell your doctor right away if you may be pregnant.
cards.missed: Take it when you remember, unless it is almost time for the next one. Never take two at once.
side: Dizzy when you stand up fast. Stand up slowly.
A stuffy nose or feeling tired in the first weeks.
Your doctor may check your kidneys and potassium with a blood test.
cards.emergency: Swelling of the face, lips or tongue, or trouble breathing: call 911.
noMix: Potassium pills or supplements.
Salt substitutes made with potassium (some "lite salt" or "low sodium salt").
Pain pills called NSAIDs, like ibuprofen, naproxen and mefenamic acid.
Lithium.
cards.food: Use herbs, calamansi and vinegar instead of salt. Read the label: many low sodium salts are made with potassium.
cards.generic: Generic name: losartan potassium. Brand names you may see: Cozaar, Lifezar.

cards.name: Metformin
cards.what: Metformin helps your body use its own insulin better and makes your liver release less sugar.
how: Take it with a meal. This helps your stomach.
Check your blood sugar as your doctor told you.
Drink water, and eat regular meals.
cards.missed: Take it with your next meal. Do not take two doses together.
side: Upset stomach, loose stools or a metal taste. These often get better after a few weeks.
After many years it can lower vitamin B12. Your doctor may check it.
cards.emergency: Strong muscle pain, trouble breathing, feeling very tired, or a lot of vomiting and stomach pain: get help now.
noMix: Heavy alcohol.
Dye used for some scans (contrast). Tell the staff you take metformin before a scan.
On sick days with vomiting, loose stools or no drinking, ask your doctor. You may need to pause it.
cards.food: Keep rice and sweets small and steady. Fish, vegetables and beans fit well.
cards.generic: Generic name: metformin hydrochloride. Brand names you may see: Glucophage.

cards.name: Atorvastatin
cards.forWhat: High cholesterol, and to lower the risk of heart attack and stroke
cards.what: Atorvastatin lowers the amount of cholesterol your liver makes. Less cholesterol means less build-up in your blood vessels.
how: Take it once a day, at any time, with or without food.
Keep taking it. You will not feel it working.
Your doctor may check your blood fats and liver with a blood test.
cards.missed: Take it when you remember that day. If it is a new day, skip it. Never take two at once.
side: Muscle aches. Tell your doctor if they are strong or do not go away.
Upset stomach or headache.
cards.emergency: Strong muscle pain with weakness or dark urine: call your doctor today.
noMix: Large amounts of grapefruit juice.
Some antibiotics, like clarithromycin and erythromycin.
Some medicines for fungus, like itraconazole.
Red yeast rice (it has a statin-like part). Ask first.
cards.food: Less fried food and fatty meat helps. Fish, beans and vegetables are good choices.
cards.generic: Generic name: atorvastatin calcium. Brand names you may see: Lipitor.

cards.name: Aspirin (low dose)
cards.forWhat: A low daily dose is sometimes used to help prevent a heart attack or stroke
cards.what: Low dose aspirin makes your blood less sticky, so clots form less easily. It can also make you bleed more easily.
how: Take it only if your doctor told you to. It is not right for everyone.
Take it with food or after a meal to help your stomach.
Swallow the tablet with water.
cards.missed: Take it when you remember that day. If it is a new day, skip it. Never take two at once.
side: Upset stomach or heartburn.
Bruising or nose bleeds more easily.
cards.emergency: Black or bloody stools, vomiting blood, or a bad headache with weakness on one side: call 911.
noMix: Ibuprofen and other NSAIDs. Ibuprofen can block the heart benefit of aspirin.
Blood thinners like warfarin.
Heavy alcohol.
Fish oil, ginkgo or high dose vitamin E can add to bleeding.
cards.food: Take it with a meal. Keep alcohol to a little or none.
cards.generic: Generic name: acetylsalicylic acid. Brand names you may see: Aspilets. Do not give aspirin to a child or teen with a fever.

cards.name: Paracetamol
cards.what: Paracetamol eases mild to moderate pain and brings down fever. It does not reduce swelling.
how: Follow the dose on the pack or from your doctor. Wait at least 4 to 6 hours between doses.
Do not go over the daily limit. Many packs say not more than 3,000 to 4,000 mg in 24 hours, so ask your pharmacist for the number that fits you.
Fever for more than 3 days: see a doctor.
cards.missed: It is taken only when needed. If you take it on a schedule, skip the missed one and never double up.
side: Rare when you take the right dose.
Too much can hurt the liver, even if you feel fine at first.
cards.emergency: Taken too much by mistake, even if you feel fine: call 911 or poison control now.
noMix: Other medicines with paracetamol. Many cold and flu medicines have it too.
Heavy alcohol.
Blood thinner warfarin: ask first if you take paracetamol often.
cards.food: It can be taken with or without food.
cards.generic: Generic name: paracetamol, also called acetaminophen. Brand names you may see: Biogesic, Tylenol.

cards.name: Ibuprofen
cards.what: Ibuprofen is a pain pill called an NSAID. It eases pain and swelling, and it brings down fever.
how: Take it with food or milk.
Use the lowest dose for the shortest time.
Ask first if you have kidney, heart or stomach problems, or high blood pressure.
cards.missed: It is taken only when needed. Never double up.
side: Stomach pain or heartburn.
It can raise blood pressure and hurt the kidneys, most of all in older people.
cards.emergency: Black stools, vomiting blood, chest pain or trouble breathing: call 911.
noMix: Other NSAIDs: naproxen, diclofenac, mefenamic acid, celecoxib.
Aspirin.
Blood pressure pills like losartan: more risk to the kidneys.
Blood thinners like warfarin.
cards.food: Take it with a meal, never on an empty stomach.
cards.generic: Generic name: ibuprofen. Brand names you may see: Advil, Medicol.

cards.name: Omeprazole
cards.forWhat: Heartburn, acid reflux and stomach ulcers
cards.what: Omeprazole lowers the acid your stomach makes, so heartburn and ulcers can heal.
how: Take it 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast, with water. Swallow the capsule whole.
Heartburn medicine from the store is for 14 days. See your doctor if you need more.
cards.missed: Take it when you remember, unless it is almost time for the next one. Never take two at once.
side: Headache, loose stools or stomach pain.
Used for a long time it can lower magnesium and vitamin B12, and may weaken bones.
cards.emergency: Black stools, vomiting blood, or trouble swallowing: call your doctor now, or 911 if it is bad.
noMix: Clopidogrel (a blood thinner for the heart): it can work less well.
Methotrexate.
Some fungus medicines, like ketoconazole: they work less well.
cards.food: Smaller meals, less fried and spicy food, and not lying down right after eating can help.
cards.generic: Generic name: omeprazole. Brand names you may see: Losec.

cards.name: Gliclazide
cards.what: Gliclazide tells your pancreas to make more insulin. This lowers blood sugar. It can also lower it too much.
how: Take it with breakfast, or as your doctor told you.
Never skip meals when you take it.
Know the signs of low sugar: shaky, sweaty, hungry, confused.
cards.missed: Take it with your next meal. Never take two doses together.
side: Low blood sugar.
Upset stomach or weight gain.
cards.emergency: Low sugar signs: take 3 teaspoons of sugar or half a cup of juice, and check again in 15 minutes. If the person is very sleepy or cannot swallow, call 911.
noMix: Alcohol.
Fluconazole and miconazole (fungus medicines): sugar can go too low.
Beta blockers like metoprolol can hide the signs of low sugar.
Other diabetes medicines, unless your doctor planned it.
cards.food: Eat at regular times. Carry a sweet snack when you go out.
cards.generic: Generic name: gliclazide. Brand names you may see: Diamicron.

cards.name: Salbutamol inhaler
cards.forWhat: Quick relief of asthma and wheezing
cards.what: Salbutamol opens the small airways in the lungs fast. It is a reliever, not a daily controller.
how: Shake it. Breathe out, press once and breathe in slowly. Hold your breath for 10 seconds.
A spacer helps more medicine reach the lungs.
cards.missed: It is used when needed, so there is no missed dose.
side: Shaky hands or a fast heartbeat for a short time.
Headache.
cards.emergency: No relief after puffs, you cannot speak a full sentence, or your lips look blue: call 911.
noMix: Beta blockers like metoprolol and propranolol can stop it working.
Some water pills can lower potassium more.
Needing more puffs than usual: tell your doctor. Asthma may be getting worse.
cards.food: No food rules. Keep it away from heat and sun.
cards.generic: Generic name: salbutamol, also called albuterol. Brand names you may see: Ventolin.

cards.name: Cetirizine
cards.forWhat: Allergies: sneezing, runny nose, itchy eyes and hives
cards.what: Cetirizine blocks histamine, the body chemical that causes allergy signs.
how: Take one tablet once a day, with or without food.
It can make you sleepy. Take it in the evening if it does.
cards.missed: It is used when needed. If you take it every day, take it when you remember. Never double up.
side: Sleepy or tired.
Dry mouth or headache.
cards.emergency: Swelling of the face, lips or tongue, or trouble breathing: call 911.
noMix: Alcohol.
Sleeping pills, and other medicines that make you sleepy.
Other allergy pills on the same day.
cards.generic: Generic name: cetirizine hydrochloride. Brand names you may see: Zyrtec, Virlix.

cards.name: Vitamin D
cards.what: Your skin makes vitamin D in the sun. Food gives a little. A pill can help when you get little sun or eat little of it. It helps your body use calcium for strong bones.
how: Take it with a meal that has some fat, so it is absorbed well.
Most adults need about 600 to 800 IU a day from all sources. The safe upper limit is 4,000 IU a day for adults.
cards.missed: Take it the next day. Never double up.
side: Usually none at normal doses.
Too much can raise calcium in the blood: nausea, weakness, a lot of urine.
cards.emergency: Vomiting, confusion or feeling very weak after taking a lot: get medical help.
noMix: Water pills called thiazides: calcium can go too high.
Steroids like prednisone: they can lower how well it works.
Cholesterol medicine cholestyramine and the weight loss pill orlistat: take vitamin D at a different time.
cards.food: Eggs, fatty fish and fortified milk have some vitamin D.
cards.generic: Also called cholecalciferol (D3). Studies on falls and other health goals give mixed results.

cards.name: Fish oil
cards.forWhat: Some people use it to lower blood fats called triglycerides
cards.what: Fish oil has omega-3 fats. Eating fish a few times a week is the best source. High dose prescription forms can lower triglycerides.
how: Take it with a meal to lessen fishy burps.
Store it in a cool place. Throw it away if it smells bad.
cards.missed: Take it the next day. Never double up.
side: Fishy taste or burps.
Upset stomach or loose stools.
High doses may add to bleeding.
cards.emergency: Black stools or bleeding that does not stop: get medical help.
noMix: Blood thinners like warfarin, and aspirin: more chance of bleeding at high doses.
Blood pressure pills: they may lower blood pressure a little more.
The weight loss pill orlistat: you may absorb less.
cards.food: Fresh sardinas, tanigue and bangus are good fish choices. Grill or steam instead of frying.
cards.generic: Look for EPA and DHA on the label.

cards.name: Calcium
cards.forWhat: Strong bones, when food does not give enough
cards.what: Calcium builds and keeps bones strong. Food is the best source. A pill can fill the gap if you eat little dairy, small fish or greens.
how: Take no more than 500 mg at one time. Split the day's amount.
Calcium carbonate works best with food. Calcium citrate can be taken any time.
Women 51 and older need about 1,200 mg a day, and men 51 to 70 about 1,000 mg, from food and pills together. The upper limit is 2,000 mg.
cards.missed: Take it with your next meal. Never double up.
side: Gas, bloating or constipation.
Too much can cause kidney stones.
cards.emergency: Strong pain in your side or blood in the urine: call your doctor.
noMix: Levothyroxine: take them 4 hours apart.
Some antibiotics, like ciprofloxacin and tetracycline: take them at different times.
Iron pills: take them at different times.
Water pills called thiazides: calcium can go too high.
cards.food: Small fish eaten with the bones, tofu, milk and malunggay have calcium.
cards.generic: Common forms: calcium carbonate and calcium citrate.

cards.name: Malunggay (moringa)
cards.what: As a food, malunggay leaves have vitamins and minerals. Studies on blood sugar and blood pressure are small and early, so it does not replace your medicine.
how: The leaves in a dish like tinola are fine for most people.
Capsules and powder are not the same as food. The amount differs from brand to brand.
cards.missed: Not needed. It is not a medicine you must take on time.
side: Loose stools or an upset stomach with a lot of leaf powder.
Roots and bark are not safe in pregnancy.
cards.emergency: Swelling of the face or trouble breathing after taking it: call 911.
noMix: It may lower blood sugar more with metformin or gliclazide.
It may lower blood pressure more with amlodipine or losartan.
It may change how some medicines are broken down. Ask your pharmacist.
cards.food: Add the leaves at the end of a soup or ginisang monggo.
cards.generic: Also called moringa. No claims about brain health, cancer or other cures.
